isoDesc: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcome(s) of its information security management system.
name: Understanding the organization and its context
notes: Conduct a formal SWOT or PESTLE analysis annually. Document internal issues (culture, resources, processes) and external issues (legal, regulatory, tech market). Review the context formally during the annual Management Review.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine interested parties that are relevant to the ISMS, the requirements of these interested parties, and which of these requirements will be addressed.
name: Understanding needs and expectations of interested parties
notes: Maintain an 'Interested Parties Register' logging internal stakeholders (staff, board) and external stakeholders (regulators, customers, vendors). Detail their specific security, privacy, and compliance requirements (e.g., SLA uptime needs, GDPR compliance).

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the boundaries and applicability of the ISMS to establish its scope.
name: Determining the scope of the information security management system
notes: Document the formal ISMS Scope Statement. Explicitly define what physical locations, business units, services, and networks are included and excluded. Ensure the scope directly addresses the context (4.1) and interested party requirements (4.2).

isoDesc: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain and continually improve an information security management system, including the processes needed and their interactions.
name: Information security management system
notes: This wraps the entire standard. Ensure processes (risk management, internal audit, incident response) interact harmoniously. Map the core processes in a high-level flowchart or operating model diagram within the ISMS Manual.

isoDesc: Top management shall demonstrate leadership and commitment with respect to the ISMS by directing and supporting persons to contribute to the effectiveness of the ISMS and promoting continual improvement.
name: Leadership and commitment
notes: Ensure senior leadership (C-Suite/Board) actively signs off on the Information Security Policy. Evidence leadership commitment through meeting minutes, budget allocations for security tools, and explicit alignment of security objectives with business strategy.

isoDesc: Top management shall establish an information security policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization and provides a framework for setting information security objectives.
name: Policy
notes: Publish a high-level 'Information Security Policy'. It must explicitly state commitment to fulfilling requirements and continual improvement. It does not need to be deeply technical—keep it accessible to all staff and publicly accessible if needed.

isoDesc: Top management shall ensure that the responsibilities and authorities for roles relevant to information security are assigned and communicated.
name: Organizational roles, responsibilities and authorities
notes: Document a formal RACI chart or Organizational Chart defining who owns the ISMS. Define role descriptions for the CISO/Security Manager, Risk Owners, Asset Owners, and the steering committee. Communicate these designations clearly.

isoDesc: When planning for the ISMS, the organization shall consider issues, requirements, and determine the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed.
name: General (Actions to address risks and opportunities)
notes: Ensure the risk assessment explicitly covers not just negative threats (risks) but positive security opportunities (e.g., migrating to a secure cloud platform to reduce physical security overhead). Tie these directly back to the context defined in 4.1.

isoDesc: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk assessment process that establishes and maintains information security risk criteria.
name: Information security risk assessment
notes: Publish a 'Risk Assessment Methodology' document. Define explicit criteria for calculating Impact and Likelihood (e.g., 5x5 matrix). Define the explicit risk acceptance threshold (e.g., 'Medium risks require mitigation plan, Low risks are accepted').

isoDesc: The organization shall define and apply an information security risk treatment process to select appropriate information security risk treatment options.
name: Information security risk treatment
notes: For every assessed risk exceeding the threshold, map it to a treatment option (Mitigate, Transfer/Insure, Avoid, Accept). Produce a formal Risk Treatment Plan (RTP). Crucially, map the chosen mitigations directly to the 93 operational controls in Annex A.

isoDesc: The organization shall produce a Statement of Applicability (SoA) that contains the necessary controls and justification for inclusions or exclusions.
name: Statement of Applicability (SoA)
notes: Draft the formal SoA spreadsheet or document. It must list all 93 controls from ISO 27001 Annex A, explicitly state 'Applicable' or 'Not Applicable', provide brief justification for either status, and map to the specific risk treatment it resolves.

isoDesc: The organization shall establish information security objectives at relevant functions and levels. The objectives shall be measurable (if practicable).
name: Information security objectives and planning to achieve them
notes: Define specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART) security objectives for the year (e.g., 'Achieve >95% completion rate of security training', 'Maintain zero critical data breaches'). Document action plans to achieve them.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine and provide the resources needed for the establishment, implementation, maintenance and continual improvement of the ISMS.
name: Resources
notes: Evidence that management has provided sufficient resources. This includes financial budget for security tools, headcount for security staffing, and dedicated time for personnel to perform risk assessments and audits.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its information security performance.
name: Competence
notes: Maintain job descriptions detailing required security qualifications for sensitive roles (e.g., CISO requires CISSP or equivalent). Maintain records of training, certifications, and education verifying staff competence.

isoDesc: Persons doing work under the organization's control shall be aware of the information security policy and their contribution to the effectiveness of the ISMS.
name: Awareness
notes: Implement mandatory annual security awareness training for all staff and contractors. Content must explicitly mention the Information Security Policy, the implications of non-compliance, and how to report incidents. Track completion metrics.

isoDesc: The organization shall determine the need for internal and external communications relevant to the information security management system.
name: Communication
notes: Draft a 'Communications Plan' that outlines: on what topics to communicate (incidents, policy updates), when to communicate, with whom (regulators, clients, staff), and who is explicitly authorized to communicate (PR, Legal, C-Suite).

isoDesc: The organization's ISMS shall include documented information required by this document and determined as necessary for the effectiveness of the ISMS.
name: Documented information
notes: Establish document control rules. Ensure every ISMS policy, procedure, and manual has a version number, author, approver, and date. Ensure confidential ISMS documents are protected from unauthorized viewing or tampering.

isoDesc: The organization shall plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet information security requirements, and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6.
name: Operational planning and control
notes: This links the planning (Clause 6) to the actual doing. Ensure the Risk Treatment Plans are actively executed. Control planned changes, and review the consequences of unintended changes, taking action to mitigate adverse effects.

isoDesc: The organization shall perform information security risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.
name: Information security risk assessment (Operational)
notes: Do not let the risk register stagnate. Formally schedule risk assessment reviews at least annually, and immediately following major architectural changes, cloud migrations, or significant security incidents. Retain documented evidence of the results.

isoDesc: The organization shall implement the information security risk treatment plan. The organization shall retain documented information of the results.
name: Information security risk treatment (Operational)
notes: Evidence the active implementation of the RTP. If a treatment was 'Deploy EDR tools by Q3', provide the project closure sign-offs or active deployed tooling proof. Retain records showing the progression and completion of risk treatments.

isoDesc: The organization shall evaluate the information security performance and the effectiveness of the ISMS. It shall determine what needs to be monitored and measured.
name: Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation
notes: Define explicit KPIs/metrics for ISMS performance (e.g., 'Phishing click rate < 5%', 'Critical patches deployed < 7 days'). Collect the data routinely and present the analysis to management to prove whether security controls are actually working.

isoDesc: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the ISMS conforms to requirements and is effectively implemented.
name: Internal audit
notes: Establish a 3-year audit programme covering all clauses and controls. Use independent auditors (internal staff outside the ISMS chain of command, or external consultants). Document the audit findings and formally assign nonconformities.

isoDesc: Top management shall review the organization's information security management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
name: Management review
notes: Conduct the 'Management Review Meeting' at least annually. Follow the strict agenda defined by ISO (review of previous actions, internal audit results, risk assessments, KPIs, continual improvement opportunities). Retain signed meeting minutes as evidence.

isoDesc: The organization shall continually improve the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the information security management system.
name: Continual improvement
notes: Evidence that the ISMS is maturing over time. Pull examples from management reviews, audit findings, and completed risk treatment plans demonstrating that the organization's security posture is stronger today than it was a year ago.

isoDesc: When a nonconformity occurs, the organization shall react to the nonconformity, evaluate the need for action to eliminate causes, and implement corrective actions.
name: Nonconformity and corrective action
notes: Maintain a 'Corrective Action Register' (CAR) or root-cause tracking system. When an internal audit, external audit, or incident reveals a failure, formally log it, perform root cause analysis (e.g., 5 Whys), assign corrective tasks, and verify they resolved the root cause.
